description: Middleware architecture hardening conformance: context namespacing, CircuitBreakerMiddleware state machine, TracingMiddleware span lifecycle, and async handler detection (Issue #42).

test_cases.description: Framework middleware writing a key with the _apcore.* prefix is valid and must not produce a warning or error.
User extension middleware writing a key with the ext.* prefix is valid and must not produce a warning or error.
User middleware attempting to write a key with the _apcore.* prefix must produce a warning or error — this is a namespace violation.
When the error rate in the rolling window exceeds open_threshold, the circuit must transition to OPEN.
A call attempted while the circuit is in OPEN state must be short-circuited and raise CircuitBreakerOpenError without reaching the module.

expected.error_class_name_is_not_the_contract: apcore-python names the class CircuitBreakerOpenError; apcore-rust has no such type, only ErrorCode::CircuitBreakerOpen. Only the wire code is assertable in all three.

test_cases.description: After recovery_window_ms has elapsed since the circuit opened, the circuit must transition to HALF_OPEN and allow exactly one probe call through.
A successful probe call in HALF_OPEN state must transition the circuit back to CLOSED and emit apcore.circuit.closed.
TracingMiddleware must create a span in before() with the correct name and mandatory attributes.
TracingMiddleware must not raise any error when the OpenTelemetry SDK is not installed; it must silently operate as a no-op.
inspect.iscoroutinefunction() must return true for an async def function and false for a plain def function.

incorrect_method_result.note: isawaitable() always returns false for uncalled functions; must not be used for async detection

driver_contract.assert_the_wire_code: Cross-language cases state their expected failure as `error_code`, the wire string, never a class name. `circuit_breaker_short_circuits_open` asserted `CircuitBreakerOpenError`, a Python/TypeScript class apcore-rust cannot have — Rust models these as `ErrorCode` variants — so no Rust driver could ever satisfy it. Cases carrying an explicit `language` field are the exception: they assert that language's API shape, and a type name there is the thing under test rather than a stand-in for the contract.
